doc: GRT smoke tier (results/grt.md, scripts/validate-increment.sh): which validation targets a changed path can reach. Every rule whose paths match a changed file adds its reach (an 'exclusive' rule that matches first ends the search: a .md anywhere reaches nothing); a changed file that NO rule matches reaches every target ('*'): conservative by default. Targets: pure (the pure self-tests, always run), lock-tests, capture-build, pnpm-test, cargo:<crate dir>, native:<gate>@<core>, g7:<group>@<receiver>, g7live:<group>@<receiver>, g7x:<group> (desktop g7-dev/g7-bench), none. '*' in a target pattern ranges over the universe below. Sabotage legs (native runs) run only when a changed path matches sabotage_paths or a changed file's content matches sabotage_content; otherwise they are skipped-by-tier (RS_SABOTAGE_TIER=skip). --milestone runs every target with sabotage.

smoke.doc: Smoke tier: the legs one representative run keeps, per group. g7live: RS_SMOKE_LEGS entries (leg directories relative to the native runner's --out; an entry also covers the directories under it), with the capture and reference legs the live leg is judged against; full_legs is the group's leg count in a full run (null: not counted). g7 (file mode): GATE7_SMOKE_LEGS, '@first' = the first non-sabotage receiver leg of each gate. A group not listed (g7-lc, g7-r, g7x, the native gates) runs whole in smoke; native gates still skip their sabotage legs unless the diff touches a checker. A change reaching collapse_at or more groups on a receiver is shared code: smoke runs the first reached group there and lists the rest in smoke_deferred (the full tier runs them). The verdict requires every named entry to have run, so a wrong name fails loudly.
smoke.defer_doc: Groups smoke never runs (the full tier and --milestone run them whole, listed in smoke_deferred): g7-k's soak legs hold the exclusive quiet lock for 300 s each (about 11 min per browser with startup), and run-gate7.sh has no leg filter for them that tier-verdict.py would accept. Run a g7-k change with --tier full --only g7live-<r>-timing.

timing_doc: GRT4a: targets whose runs go in validate-increment.sh's last phase, after every correctness run: their exclusive quiet-lock legs (gate 6's g6l/g6s/g6c/g6p, the timing live groups, the bench and device-control arms) starved the browser groups sharing a tier with them (G7q: 11.9-13.8 ks of summed lock wait). A receiver's live groups split into a correctness run and a -timing run.

remote.doc: scripts/remote-validate.sh (docs/remote-compute.md): which planned runs may go to hosted runners at the current rung. A run is remote-capable when its id matches a 'capable' glob and nothing in 'refuse' applies; 'refuse' always wins. 'refuse.groups' refuses single groups of a gate 7 run (the run keeps its other groups remotely, and is refused whole when none is left). Every other run is refused with default_reason (each rung widens 'capable'). Refused runs are listed in the summary's remote.refused[] and may be run locally with --and-local.
remote.capable_doc: G8g: gate 8's browser group g7-8 (its file legs in g7-gsw/g7-web-rust and its live g8l legs in g7live-gsw/g7live-web-rust) is remote-capable: --determinism 2,1 (run 40088061009) agreed over 12 runs, 205/205 shots and 70/70 dumps. R4: bench-instr (cachegrind Ir per golden case; load-insensitive, so not a timing run). R3: gate 7's browser correctness runs on the CI-only lavapipe renderer (lib/browser-renderer.ts): the file groups (every timing group of their native sources skipped by RS_SKIP_TIMING_GROUPS) and the live correctness groups g7-5 and g7-55 (refuse.groups keeps g7-1 and g7-2 local: on a 4-vCPU runner each failed a check intermittently from credit-window-2 timing, load-sensitive, so local-only and never loosened). Every -timing run (g7-6, g7-lc, g7-r, g7-k) is refused by phase, g7x by id, device legs by match; the native receiver has no live correctness run (run-gate7.sh runs g7-r only there).

g7live-*.g7-1: G7rf fixed the receivers' resync-at-fold bug (a fold holding the forced full ends the wait; gate1-g1d-checks.ts checkResyncFull passes 5/5 locally on gsw and web at window 2), but the remote determinism check (run 39982714414, --determinism 3,1) still disagrees on GSW: one runner's live-resync leg shot no step 2 (its a704118930 image, and the step-2 diff, are absent; every check passed), so it is a shot-window miss under runner load before the resync, not the resync wait. Web-rust agreed over 4 runs (519/519 shots). Local-only until the GSW step-2 window miss is understood

gate 8 opt-in seams (G8w): the adoption and texture-decode seams, the gate 8 policy parser and their ctests. Their call sites in entry.cpp and hooks.cpp are shared capture files and still reach '*'; a change confined to these files cannot move a /2-/7 run, so the build, the pure self-tests, the default gate 0 leg and gate 8 (whose g8t/g8a legs run these seams) are enough. G8a added native:gate8@* and rs_adopt_test.cpp

texture workers (G8kw, texture-delivery-design.md D11, Q7): the pool, the publication hold-back and their ctest. Off unless GRC_TEXTURE_WORKERS=<N>, which only gate 8's g8t workers legs set, so a change confined to these files moves no /2-/7 run and no synchronous capture: the build (whose ctests drive this code), the pure self-tests, the default gate 0 leg and gate 8 are enough. Their call sites in hooks.cpp, rs_mirror.cpp, rs_resource_log.cpp and entry.cpp are shared capture files and still reach '*'

texture delivery seam, the lazy Basis encode jobs and the /9 codec test (G8k9, G8kp, G8ku; texture-delivery-design.md D1, D6, D12, Q5): the delivery policy, the variants it offers (block under passthrough and basis-uastc, uastc under basis-uastc), the D12 rules, the encode pool and job runner (rs_texture_basis), and rs9_codec_test. Every variant is off unless GRC_STREAM_VERSION=9 with a GRC_TEXTURE_DELIVERY mode other than rgba, which no run outside gate 8 sets, so a change confined to these files moves no /2-/8 run: the build (whose ctests drive them), the pure self-tests, the default gate 0 leg and gate 8 are enough. Their call sites in entry.cpp and rs_mirror.cpp are shared capture files and still reach '*'

the vendored basisu encoder and its wrapper (G8kv, texture-delivery-design.md D13, D15): only G8ku's encode jobs (rs_texture_basis, under a /9 basis-uastc stream) call rs_basis_encode, so a change confined to these files moves no other capture output. They are built into the capture library and driven by rs_basis_encode_test and the Godot-transcoder round trip (rs_basis_roundtrip), both ctests in the build, and by gate 8's g8ku legs: the build, the pure self-tests, the default gate 0 leg and gate 8 are enough. G8ku dropped capture/CMakeLists.txt from this rule (it now links rs_texture_basis into the capture, a shared file's reach) and added its level bench and the bench's PNG converter

the persisted host texture cache and the prepare step (G8kc, texture-delivery-design.md D7-D10): the cache module and its ctest, and the prepare script with its headless Godot script. The cache is closed unless GRC_TEXTURE_CACHE_DIR is set, which only gate 8's g8kc legs and prepare-textures.sh set, so a change confined to these files moves no other gate: the build (whose ctests drive the cache), the pure self-tests, the default gate 0 leg and gate 8 are enough. Their call sites (hooks.cpp, entry.cpp, rs_resource_log.h) and the calibration record are shared capture files and still reach '*'
